Name: Dave Haynie
Question: What is your reaction to Eric Trump saying that lenders "laughed" at his family's $454 million bond request?
Answer: Maybe a rare bit of truth from a Trump family member. Trump make pleas from to 30 different Assurance related companies. Not one would offer money, despite Trump offering up business records (which at least in some cases proved to be locked and unavailable for their use). These companies, usually insurance companies, have the control of billions of dollars. They absolutely could come up with the promise of the money — they don’t have to provide the cash until the appeals are over and only if Trump were to lose. Why didn’t they? Several possible reasons. So what are Trump’s options? If he doesn’t come up with the money, New York State will immediately start asset forfeiture proceedings, and he’ll have given up his option of filing an appeal. That changes things, since now there’s no question about Trump owing the money, no chance to have the dollar value reduced. He could declare bankruptcy. That would likely be very bad, politically, but it could pause at least some of the legal proceedings coming his way, it would slow the process way, way down, and it would move the dissolution of his properties into bankruptcy court rather than being under the auspices of the current civil court. But it would also automatically trigger default on all kind of loans he’s already got, causing a complete meltdown of his “empire” as every creditor scrambles to get as close to full dollar on their loans as possible. It’s been suggested, and that is how Rudy Giuliani and Alex Jones ducked their legal liabilities after losing their cases. But it’s also true that legal judgements are handled differently than regular debt, and Trump would not likely be able to reduce that judgement. The bankruptcy could also see the court put ahead of other creditors. [5] And either way, he’s losing those assets. The sell off could be more favorable under the terms of bankruptcy, but they would still happen. UPDATE 35-March-2024 Just in time to save Trump’s ego, a New York Appeals Court lowered the amount that Trump must post in advance of his appeal being granted, and gave him an additional ten days to produce either the cash or a bond that covers the full amount. [6] There is no indication so far that the Appeals Court has actually lowered the total amount of the fine, they’re apparently just allowing a “good faith” down payment. Because, of course, everyone else’s rules don’t apply to Trump. I guess he finally got something for those hundreds of millions he’s spent in legal fees these last few years!

Name: Dave Haynie
Question: How has Rush Limbaugh achieved success in the talk radio industry despite the rise of the internet?
Answer: You can follow the rise of Limbaugh and see pretty much where he intersects the Internet. Some early experiments that would eventually lead to some of the Internet technologies — packet switching networks — were begun in 1969. Rush Limbaugh entered broadcasting as a DJ at WIXZ Radio, a Top 40 Station in Pennsylvania, back in 1971, using the on-air name “Bachelor Jeff,” and was basically trying to sound like Don Imus. He was fired after only eighteen months. About this time, a few colleges had been connected using the early Arpanet protocols that came out of those first experiments. He found another job, this time in Pittsburgh, but didn’t last a year there. In 1974, he temporarily left radio and want back to living with his parents. The first efforts to develop a more powerful “inter-network” to support large de-centralized networks that year, eventually leading to the TCP/IP protocol, one of the foundations of the internet. A year, in 1975, later he got an afternoon DJ gig at KUDL in Kansas City, Missouri, but was also able to host a weekend public affairs talk show. He lasted two years at this gig, was fired, and landed for a short gig at a competing radio station. Also in 1975, Email had become one of the killer applications on the early emerging Internet, still pretty much a research thing. Limbaugh left radio in 1979 and became a salesman for the Kansas City Royals. He didn’t go back to broadcasting until 1983, when he got a talk slot at KMBZ AM radio in Kansas City. His show didn’t last long, he was soon fired. But shortly thereafter, he found a position as the replacement for radio celebrity Morton Downy Jr. on KFBK radio in Sacramento, California. He decided to use his real name at this gig, and by 1985 he was “getting political” on the air. During these years, Usenet was invented (it’s a nerd thing), Arpanet had switched to TCP/IP protocols, and the Domain Name System (DNS) was invented. That latter is another one of the keys to enabling the modern internet. Also, Q-Link (aka Quantum Link) launched in 1985. Also in 1985, 1200 baud modems (V.22) overtook 300 baud as the most common used by consumers (I had a 1200 baud modem in 1982… thanks Bell Labs!). Oh, and that Fairness Doctrine thing? Conservative media company Capitol Cities had managed a leveraged buyout of the American Broadcasting System (ABC) in 1985. Not at all coincidentally, the FCC dropped enforcement of the Fairness Doctrine in 1985 — this is what allowed Limbaugh to get political without repercussions. See, as part of its purchase, Capitol Cities would own the ABC Radio Network, including a bunch of failing AM stations. So Capitol Cities had the idea to turn those toward selling conservative propaganda! If they couldn’t make money directly, they could sell Conservative notions — like tax cuts for the rich — to the hicks and poor people sill using AM radio, a thing that had largely fallen out use for music and anything else requiring a quality sound. So Capitol Cities used their political pull, put in their choice of FCC Chairman, and had just that one request… to start with. So propaganda would now be fully legal without any silly “equal time” mandates. And the Fairness Doctrine was fully rescinded by 1987. In 1988, ABC Radio Network offered Limbaugh both a local talk spot on WABC Radio in New York City — Limbaugh had done well enough in California that he could require a Top 5 city job in this next move. He was also given a nationally syndicated show… and thus, AM Hate Radio was born. Internet-wise the IRC protocol was launched in 1988 (that’s the protocol for chat rooms on the Internet). Also in 1988, the 2400 band modem (V.22bis) was the popular choice for dialup internet services. By 1990, Rush Limbaugh had “more listeners than any other talk show host. He was nationally syndicated now in major markets, eventually hitting 650 markets. The World Wide Web — what some people think of as “the internet” — was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. The first commercial dial-up ISPs were also founded in 1989. Yup, before then, you probably only used the internet at work or at a college. You get get 9,600 baud modems (V.32) in 1990, but they were expensive! Limbaugh was so powerful in US Right Wing Politics in 1992 that George H. W. Bush personally invited him for a stay-over in the Lincoln Bedroom, as Limbaugh was a Pat Buchanan supporter. Also in 1992, first photograph was uploaded, a GIF file of “the Horrible CERN Girls.” The V.32bis standard brought the 14.4kb/s modem this year as well. It wouldn’t be until 1994 when XXYC, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, became the first US radio station to offer continuous internet streaming. This was a year after RTHK (Radio Television Hong Kong) has launched a similar radio streaming service. Simply put, people who became famous in media prior to modern streaming media services did that based on traditional media: radio, television, film, and performance. The latter, at least, is still a big part of one’s path to fame.

Name: Dave Haynie
Question: Is it necessary to apply for a provisional patent before starting production if you plan on selling products online?
Answer: Nope. You don’t have to patent anything. If you have something unique done in your widget, you might be able to patent it. And it’s also possible your widget is going to infringe on existing patents. You’d do well to do a patent search. A provisional patent is really just a place holder. It does lock in your date-of-application, and it lets you say “patent pending,” but otherwise it’s not too meaningful. It lasts a year, by which is needs to either be replaced by a general patent, or tossed out. In the USA, a patent has to be filed within a year of disclosing your invention, though in many countries, disclosure of your invention prevents it from being patented. You probably file the provisional patent as an exercise in starting your general patent, and to give your team some extra time to finish the general patent. Note that a provisional patent is not examined. The PTO checks to ensure you filled out the paperwork correctly, but they don’t go into examining the invention for patentability. The provisional can’t be used to sue someone in court. It’s well understood to be going away within the year unless you complete the general patent. Selling online has absolutely nothing to do with it. Unless, of course, you wrote your own sales interface to sell your widgets online, and you’ve stepped on other recent e-commerce patents.

Question: A liberal man will ruin your life. Why don’t people understand conservative men train to fight, and protect women?
Answer: Hey there Deven, aka Anonymous Coward. Didn’t you get the message that a real man uses his real name, rather than hiding behind a fake or incomplete one. Though with all the trolling you do, it’s no wonder. You really don’t know the first thing about women, do you? You also apparently have a “hot” husband… I’m getting mixed signals here. As for your question, I’m about as liberal as they come, and while I don’t generally run into situations in which my wife or my daughter need me to fight for them, I do know how to fight. That’s three years of Judo and six years of Aikido. Doesn’t hurt that I’m also 6ft tall and no lightweight. But here’s the thing: I’m no caveman. Of course I protect my people… I learned this as a kid with three younger sisters. It’s as natural to me as riding a bike or snorkeling. I can defend them with my physical ability, with my trained knowledge of self-defense, but in civilization, also with my mind. That means that in the 44 years since I met my wife, she’s never been attacked by anyone. Because we’re not going into those kind of situations in the first place. That’s what an good man does. He doesn’t intentionally put any of his family or friends in unnecessary danger. So he works hard and provides a good income, so they can live in civilized parts of the world, He ensures the family has reliable vehicles that don’t break down in bad neighborhoods or strand them in remote locations. Well, that and an AAA membership… again, civilization has its advantages. Kid, if you ever do get a girlfriend — my Magic 8 Ball says “very doubtful” — you’re not going to protect her from a gang of thugs if you take her to where those thugs are. You won’t be enough. And I’m thinking, if you’re the typical fake Alpha male, you’ll leave her behind while you run away. After all, she’s just a female, eh? That’s the caveman thinking I usually get from your kind, but maybe you’re different. Maybe not. As angry as you sound, who’s going to protect her from you? Spousal abuse and other domestic violence is highest in the most conservative areas of the country. And what training? How often have you actually practiced folks twice your size? Against multiple attackers? And how many.. two, three, more? In my Aikido school, we went up to six. Yeah, it’s just practice… the attackers only hit, they didn’t grapple or use weapons. No one is intentionally hurt, lots of pain but no broken bones. Otherwise we run out of practice partners. And I got pretty good at releasing chokes before my Uke passed out. We did our weapons practice one on one.. that can be dangerous even with a wooden tanto, bokken or jo, much less live blades. I do recommend Aikido if you can find a good school that practices it hard. It takes dedication to learn. And years. But it’s worth it.
